title: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report — US crude, gasoline and distillate stocks (10:30 ET, decision-day morning)
source: EST: eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/ fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200) states the date verbatim — 'Data for week ending Sep. 4, 2026 / Release Date: Sep. 10, 2026 / Next Release Date: Sep. 16, 2026'. Cross-checked against eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/schedule.php, also fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200): the standard release is 'after 10:30 a.m. eastern time on Wednesday', and the 2026 rows of its Holiday Release Schedule name exceptions ONLY for the weeks ending 01-16, 02-13, 05-22, 09-04, 10-09 and 11-06 — the week ending 09-11 is not among them, so the standard rule applies unmodified. This UPGRADES the evidence behind proposals/eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-16.from-fomc-2026-09-16.json (2026-09-10), which derived 09-16 from the publisher's stated rule plus weekday arithmetic: the publisher now names the date itself on its own landing page. Status stays `estimate` on ONE count, and it is not date doubt — the confirmed-prefix table in market-events-data.ts defines NO prefix for an EIA release schedule (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:), the same schema gap ftc-v-amazon-antitrust-trial-2027-03-29 and google-adtech-opinion-unseal-2026-09-16 documented for a federal court docket. An `EIA:` prefix would confirm this event and every eia-steo-* entry on the calendar; adding one is a schema change, not this lane's call. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH, 2026-09-15 (D-1), after reading the one proposal that named this id (proposals/eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-16.from-fomc-2026-09-16.json, filed by the FOMC lane on 2026-09-10). That proposal's ATTRIBUTION reason is adopted unchanged and is the whole reason this event is tracked: the calendar carries the monthly oil reports bracketing the FOMC corridor (eia-steo-2026-09-09, opec-momr-2026-09-10, iea-omr-2026-09-11) but not the weekly US inventory print that lands INSIDE it, 10:30 ET on the morning of the 14:00 ET statement. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is tiered low deliberately: no house playbook is energy-keyed, no tracked symbol carries direct crude exposure, and `symbols` is left EMPTY on purpose — populating it with XLE/USO would assert an exposure this lane does not have. Measured this session and load-bearing for the stance: the prior print (2026-09-10, 12:00 ET on the Labor Day shift) was bearish on every headline — commercial crude -0.390 Mbbl against a -1.554 Mbbl consensus, gasoline +1.269, distillate +2.086 — and WTI still closed +6.69% (96.05 -> 102.48) with Brent +6.34%. In a supply-shock regime the weekly print is not the price-setter; Hormuz is. Full ledger with sources: docs/research/events/eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-16.md. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
